Privacy Support

Everlight Digital Privacy Policy

Last updated: May 19, 2026  ·  Effective: May 19, 2026

Everlight Digital LLC ("we", "us", "our") publishes a family of mobile apps and web services. This Privacy Policy explains what information we collect, how we use it, and your rights. It applies to all products we publish, including:

  • Olive — family organizer (tasks, meals, calendars, Kid Mode)
  • Halcyon — weather app with radar
  • Shepherd — pastoral-care platform for churches (web service at shepherd.everlight-digital.com)
  • Tally — zero-based envelope budgeting for individuals and couples (in development)
  • Persue Bible — Bible reader with reading plans
  • Persue Prayer — prayer journal and devotional app
  • Regen — recovery and training-load dashboard
  • WordFind — daily word-search puzzle

App-specific addenda are linked at the bottom of this page where an app's data practices differ materially from the defaults described here.

1. Information We Collect

We collect only the information needed to operate the apps. The categories vary by app.

Account Information

When you sign in to apps that require an account (Olive, Persue Bible, Persue Prayer), we receive:

  • Email address
  • Name (if provided by Sign in with Apple or Google)
  • An authentication identifier issued by Apple, Google, or our auth provider
  • A hashed password (only when you sign up with email/password)

Halcyon, Regen, and WordFind do not require an account.

Content You Create

Tasks, notes, lists, calendar events, meals, recipes, grocery items, journal entries, prayer entries, sermon notes, reading-plan progress, marked verses, kid points, rewards, celebrations, habits, voice recordings, meeting transcripts, check-in entries, and similar items you save inside an app.

Health and Fitness Data (Regen only)

If you grant HealthKit permission, Regen reads heart-rate variability (HRV), resting heart rate (RHR), sleep, active energy, workouts, and body mass from Apple Health. This data stays on your device and is never transmitted to our servers. See Section 5.

Location Data (Halcyon only)

If you grant location permission, Halcyon uses your location to fetch local weather. We do not store your location on our servers. See Section 6.

Device and Diagnostic Data

Device model, iOS/iPadOS/watchOS version, app version, time zone, locale, and crash logs (via Firebase Crashlytics or Apple's standard crash reporting).

Usage Analytics

Anonymous event data (which screens are viewed, which features are tapped) via Firebase Analytics. Currently active in Olive only. Disabled by default until you accept the in-app prompt. Disabled at all times in Kid Mode. Other apps may add anonymous analytics in future versions, with notice.

Subscription and Purchase Data

Apple receives your purchase information when you subscribe via in-app purchase. RevenueCat receives a pseudonymous identifier and your subscription status to manage entitlements across devices.

App Tracking Transparency (ATT)

Apps that show ads (currently Halcyon, and WordFind if/when ads are enabled) prompt for App Tracking Transparency permission. If you grant it, the IDFA may be used by Google AdMob for personalized ads. If you decline, you still see ads, but they are non-personalized.

2. How We Use Information

  • To provide the core features of each app
  • To authenticate you and identify your subscription status
  • To sync your content across your devices (where the app supports sync)
  • To generate AI responses you request (apps with AI features)
  • To send notifications you have enabled
  • To diagnose crashes, fix bugs, and improve the apps
  • To deliver in-app purchases and manage subscriptions
  • To deliver ads (free tier of apps that show ads)
  • To comply with legal obligations

3. How We Share Information

We do not sell your personal information. We do not share your content for third-party advertising. We share data only with the service providers listed in Section 4, only as needed to operate the apps, and only under contracts that require them to protect your data.

We may disclose information when required by law, to enforce our terms, to protect rights or safety, or as part of a business transfer (with notice).

5. Health and Sensitive Data

Regen reads health data from Apple HealthKit when you grant permission. Health data is processed entirely on-device. We do not transmit, store, or share your HealthKit data.

You can revoke HealthKit access at any time in iOS Settings > Privacy & Security > Health > Regen.

Persue Prayer's mortification (sin tracking) entries and accountability check-ins are sensitive personal-reflection content. They are excluded from Spotlight indexing and stored in your private iCloud (CloudKit) container.

Tally Financial Data (Plaid)

Tally users on the Pro tier may optionally connect a bank, credit card, or other financial account through Plaid to import transactions into their budget. When you connect an account:

  • Plaid Link runs inside Tally. You authenticate directly with your financial institution through Plaid; Tally never sees your bank credentials.
  • Plaid returns a token which our Cloudflare Worker (tally-finance-worker) exchanges for an access token. The access token is encrypted at rest in Cloudflare Workers KV, keyed per user. No copy of the token is stored on your device or in our other systems.
  • Tally requests only the Plaid Transactions product. We do not request Auth, Identity, Investments, Liabilities, Income, or Assets. Tally cannot initiate ACH transfers or move money.
  • For each transaction we receive amount, merchant name, posted date, account name, and Plaid's category suggestion. These are stored inside the user's iCloud (CloudKit) shared household zone so both spouses can categorize them.
  • Disconnecting a bank inside Tally deletes the Plaid item and the stored access token immediately. Previously-imported transactions remain inside the user's CloudKit budget data until the user deletes them or removes the household.

6. Location Data

Halcyon requests location permission to fetch local weather. Your location is sent to Apple WeatherKit (and RainViewer for radar) to retrieve forecast data. We do not retain location on our servers. You can deny or revoke permission in iOS Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services.

7. AI Features

Olive (Olive Assistant: NL quick-add, Smart Weekly Review, meal AI) includes AI features powered by Anthropic's Claude API.

When you use an AI feature, the text or audio you submit is sent over HTTPS to our server (Google Cloud Functions), then forwarded to Anthropic. The response is returned to your device. We do not store your prompts or responses after the request completes. Anthropic processes the data per its commercial terms; Anthropic does not train its models on data sent through the Claude API by default.

Audio captured for transcription is converted to text on-device or via Apple Speech where possible. Audio is not stored on our servers.

8. Advertising

Halcyon's free tier shows ads via Google AdMob. You can remove ads by upgrading to the paid tier. WordFind ships with ad code stubbed; if ads become active in a future version, an in-app notice and updated policy section will explain.

If you grant App Tracking Transparency, AdMob may use your advertising identifier (IDFA) to personalize ads. If you deny, you still see ads, but they are non-personalized. See Google's ad policies.

9. Children

Olive Kid Mode

Olive supports family use. When a parent enables Kid Mode, the app is restricted to a child-safe view, Firebase Analytics is fully disabled, and only an explicit allowlist of low-risk events would ever be considered for a future release. Children sign in via the parent account; Olive does not create separate child accounts and does not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13.

Shepherd (church accounts)

Shepherd is a business-to-business service used by churches. A church may store information about minors (for example a child's name, photo, birthday, grade, gender, household, and guardian relationships) as part of its pastoral-care records. Children do not register or use Shepherd themselves — all data is entered by the church's adult staff or volunteers, or synced from the church's own church-management system; Shepherd has no child-facing accounts and collects no information directly from children. For this minor data the church is the data controller and is responsible for obtaining any parental or guardian consent required by law (e.g. COPPA, or GDPR/UK GDPR children's-data rules); Everlight is a processor acting on the church's instructions. See the Shepherd section below.

Other Apps

Halcyon, Persue Bible, Persue Prayer, Regen, and WordFind are not directed to children under 13 and do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13. If we learn we have inadvertently collected such information, we will delete it.

Parents who believe a child has provided personal information should contact brendan@everlight-digital.com.

10. Data Retention and Deletion

We retain your account data while your account is active. Apps with a Trash feature (Olive) keep deleted items for 30 days, then permanently remove them.

You can delete your account from within each app (Settings > Account > Delete Account, or the equivalent). Account deletion removes your identity record and your Firestore data within 30 days. Backups are purged within 90 days. Apple CloudKit data is controlled by you and removed when you delete it from your iCloud account or uninstall the app.

Anonymous diagnostic data (crash logs, analytics events) is retained for up to 14 months.

11. Your Rights

European Union, United Kingdom, and Switzerland (GDPR, UK GDPR)

You have the right to:

  • Access the personal data we hold about you
  • Request correction of inaccurate data
  • Request erasure ("right to be forgotten")
  • Request restriction of processing
  • Receive your data in a portable format
  • Object to processing
  • Lodge a complaint with your supervisory authority

Our legal bases for processing are: performance of contract (delivering the app you purchased), consent (location, HealthKit, analytics, ATT), and legitimate interest (security, fraud prevention, product improvement).

California (CCPA / CPRA)

California residents have the right to know what personal information we collect, to request deletion, to correct inaccurate data, to opt out of "sale" or "sharing" of personal information (we do not sell or share for cross-context behavioral advertising), and not to be discriminated against for exercising these rights.

How to Exercise Your Rights

Email brendan@everlight-digital.com from the email address tied to your account. We will respond within the timeframe required by law (30 days for GDPR, 45 days for CCPA, extendable as permitted).

12. Security

All network requests use HTTPS (TLS). Authentication tokens are stored in iOS Keychain. Server data is encrypted at rest. AI requests pass through a server proxy so the Anthropic API key is never embedded in the app. We follow industry best practices but no system is 100% secure; we cannot guarantee absolute security.

If we learn of a breach affecting your data, we will notify you without undue delay where required by law.

13. International Transfers

Our service providers (Apple, Google, Anthropic, RevenueCat) are headquartered in the United States and operate global infrastructure. If you use the apps from outside the United States, your data may be processed in the U.S. or other jurisdictions. We rely on Standard Contractual Clauses or equivalent safeguards where required.

14. Changes to This Policy

We may update this policy as the apps evolve. Material changes will be announced in-app and the "Last updated" date at the top will change. Continued use after the effective date of an update constitutes acceptance.

16. Shepherd (Churches)

Shepherd is a pastoral-care web platform used by churches (each a "Church" or "tenant"). It differs from our consumer apps, so this section governs it specifically. The canonical site is shepherd.everlight-digital.com.

Controller and processor

The Church decides what information about its members and community to store in Shepherd. For that congregant information, the Church is the data controller and Everlight is a data processor acting only on the Church's instructions. The Church is responsible for its lawful basis and for any notices or consents owed to those people (including parental consent for minors). Everlight is the controller only for the limited account/billing data needed to run the service. This Privacy Policy together with our Terms forms the data-processing agreement between the Church and Everlight; a separately signed DPA is available on request.

Categories of personal data

  • Identity & contact: names, emails, phone numbers, postal addresses, profile photos.
  • Demographic & household: date of birth/birthday, anniversary, school grade, gender, child/minor flag, family relationships, household membership, guardian links.
  • Pastoral care content (sensitive): care notes, prayer requests, pastoral-contact records, care status (e.g. hospital, grieving, at-risk), milestones (baptism, surgery, death/memorial), tasks, tags — often including health-related and other sensitive detail.
  • SMS content: if enabled, the body of inbound text messages and the sender's phone number, stored as notes.
  • Account & security: staff email and name, a bcrypt-hashed password, session data.
  • Device & technical: web-push tokens/keys and user-agent (if notifications are enabled), server logs (IP, user agent, timestamps), and the end-user IP checked by our bot-protection provider at sign-up/login.
  • Integration tokens: encrypted access/refresh tokens for a connected church-management system (e.g. Planning Center).
  • Billing: billing-contact email and a Stripe customer/subscription ID (no card numbers stored).

Minors

A Church may store data about minors as part of its care records. Children do not register or use Shepherd; adults enter all data or it syncs from the Church's church-management system. The Church is the controller of that data and is responsible for any required parental/guardian consent (COPPA, GDPR/UK GDPR children's-data rules). Parents with questions should contact their church directly; Everlight will assist the church.

Text messaging (SMS), consent & opt-out

If a Church enables SMS, message content and sender numbers are stored as notes and processed by Twilio over the carrier network. Churches must comply with applicable messaging laws (U.S. TCPA, carrier A2P 10DLC): message only consenting recipients, identify the church, and honor opt-out/help. Recipients can reply STOP to opt out and HELP for help; message and data rates may apply.

Sub-processors (Shepherd)

  • Railway — hosting + Postgres database (US region).
  • Cloudflare R2 — encrypted off-site database backups.
  • Stripe — billing/payments (card data direct to Stripe).
  • Planning Center — one-way roster sync incl. minors' data, when connected (never writes back).
  • Twilio — inbound SMS, when enabled.
  • Resend — transactional/reminder email (may include a name + short pastoral excerpt).
  • Cloudflare (Turnstile) — bot protection (receives end-user IP).
  • Google — optional sign-in.

Security, retention & rights (Shepherd)

Data is encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest; off-site R2 backups are encrypted; staff passwords are stored only as bcrypt hashes; integration tokens are encrypted before storage. Church data is retained for the life of the account; on tenant purge, live data is deleted, and encrypted backups expire on a rolling basis within 30 days. If a connected church-management system remains linked, deleted records can be re-created on the next sync (that system is the source of the roster). Because the Church is the controller, members exercise access/correction/deletion/portability rights through their Church, which administers the records; Everlight assists the Church. Shepherd is hosted in the U.S.; where required, the Church and Everlight are responsible for an appropriate cross-border transfer mechanism. On a breach affecting Church data, Everlight notifies the Church (controller) without undue delay so it can meet its own notification duties.
